newsitem.title: USA: California county loses suit for beating Mexicans.
newsitem.headline: California county loses suit for beating Mexicans.

text.p: Two illegal immigrants who were beaten by police after a high speed freeway chase will get $740,000 under an agreement reached on Friday between the American Civil Liberties Union and Riverside County.

Mark Rosenbaum, legal director for the ACLU of southern California, told reporters the settlement would be split equally between Mexican nationals Enrique Funes Flores and his girlfriend, Alicia Sotero Vasquez.

Their beating on April 1 last year by two Riverside County Sheriff's deputies was captured on videotape by a television news crew in a helicopter and sparked public outrage over police violence after it was aired nationally.
The settlement "delivers an unmistakable message that in this country we do not enforce our immigration laws by means of hard batons and racial epithets," Rosenbaum told reporters.

Funes Flores and Sotero Vasquez were among more than a dozen immigrants in a pickup truck that was chased at high speed by Riverside County Sheriff's deputies for more than 60 miles (100 km) from the Riverside County town of Temecula to the Los Angeles suburb of El Monte.

When the chase ended, most of the immigrants, who had apparently been picked up by the truck after crossing the Mexican border into California illegally, tried to flee. But Funes Flores and Sotero Vasquez stayed with the vehicle and were seen being clubbed repeatedly with batons by the two deputies.
